input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer of fifteen percent of annual Fees for each week an invoice is late — triggered by a minor payment delay and capable of exceeding the remaining contract value within weeks, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback (the only permitted Customer-payable liquidated amount is a sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated amount, penalty, or minimum termination fee exists: § 9.4 lets us terminate without cause owing only accrued Fees with a refund of prepaid Fees, and § 27 termination is expressly "without penalty". We therefore took the preferred position and replaced the § 7.7 formula with an unconditional statement that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties, leaving the rest of § 7 (including the withholding and interest mechanics in § 7.3) untouched.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable late-payment liquidated damages and state that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, particularly at fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a late invoice, so we replaced § 7.7 with our preferred position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer. If a liquidated amount is unavoidable, our fallback is a sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.oldText: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
